claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 benefits from strong Zr–B and B–B bonding.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 specimens produced at approximately 1700 °C without Si have insufficient densification.
Insufficient densification and intergranular sealing cause poor oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance in lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
Adding less than about 5 wt% Si during reactive sintering near 1700 °C induces a transient liquid phase.
The Si-induced transient liquid phase enhances particle rearrangement and bonding.
The transient liquid-phase mechanism increases densification of ZrB2 processed near 1700 °C.
Si addition produces an in situ borosilicate, silicide, or glassy intergranular phase.
Upon cooling, the liquid phase segregates to ZrB2 grain boundaries and becomes continuous.
The intergranular phase seals grain boundaries and voids.
The continuous intergranular layer impedes oxygen penetration.
The continuous intergranular layer impedes penetration by liquid plating metal.
Si-doped ZrB2 processed near 1700 °C will have mechanical strength and structural integrity at least comparable to conventionally processed ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have better liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature Si-free specimens.
The proposed processing route is applicable near 1700 °C under inert or reducing atmospheres.
The proposed material is expected to retain its oxidation and corrosion benefits in service up to approximately 1500 °C.
